claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

hospital_abroad.description: Whether the child is in hospital abroad.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 3 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask you a few questions about your situation to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now let me ask:

**Do you live with Alex, or do you contribute financially to his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards things like his clothes and food.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To understand your situation better:

**How much do you contribute financially towards Alex's upkeep each week or month?**

(I'm asking this because to qualify for Child Benefit when a child doesn't live with you, you need to contribute at least the same amount as the Child Benefit payment, which is currently around £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, or about £111 per month.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute £50 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information. Now I need to understand:

**Who does Alex currently live with? And is that person claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

(This is important because only one person can get Child Benefit for a child at any given time.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with his mum, my ex-partner. I'm not sure if she's claiming Child Benefit for him or not.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Let me ask one more important question:

**Is Alex in any special circumstances, such as being in hospital, in care, or living in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually Alex is in hospital - he's abroad in a hospital.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. That's an important detail. Let me ask some follow-up questions about this:

**How long has Alex been in the hospital abroad, and do you know how much longer he's expected to stay there?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure of all the details to be honest - it's been quite complicated with him being abroad for treatment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand this must be a difficult situation. Let me ask a couple more specific questions to help determine eligibility:

1. **Did Alex go abroad specifically for hospital treatment, or was he already abroad for other reasons when he went into hospital?**

2. **Have you been regularly spending money on Alex while he's been in the hospital abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about those details - it's all been quite confusing with everything that's happened.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - these situations can indeed be very confusing and stressful. Let me ask one final question:

**Do you know if Alex has been in the hospital for more than 12 weeks?**

(This is relevant because Child Benefit can be affected if a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks, though there are exceptions.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't really know exactly how long it's been to be honest.

Thank you for providing all the information you have. Based on our conversation, I'm unable to make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Summary of your situation:**

While you meet some of the basic requirements (you live in the UK, Alex is 3 years old, and you contribute £50 per week which exceeds the Child Benefit threshold), there are several important factors that need clarification:

1. **Another potential claimant**: Alex lives with his mother, and only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child. It's unclear whether she is already claiming.

2. **Hospital abroad circumstances**: Alex is in a hospital abroad, and special rules apply. Child Benefit may continue for children hospitalized abroad, but only if:
   - The child went abroad specifically for hospital treatment
   - You (the claimant) are back in the UK
   - You regularly spend money on them
   
3. **Duration of hospital stay**: If a child is in hospital for more than 12 weeks, it can affect Child Benefit entitlement (though exceptions exist).

**What you should do:**

I recommend that you **contact the Child Benefit Office directly** at HMRC. They can:
- Check if Alex's mother is currently claiming
- Assess your specific situation regarding Alex's hospitalization abroad
- Provide guidance on whether you're eligible to claim or continue claiming

You can reach them by phone or post through the [HMRC Child Benefit contact service](https://www.gov.uk/contact/hm-revenue-customs/child-benefit).
